topic: There is no Dutch equivalent of the Danish conversion table
text:
A student arriving from the Danish system will look for the table that turns IB points into a local average, and there is not one. Nuffic describes the IB scale and states that a full Diploma is comparable to a VWO diploma, and stops there.

That is not an omission, it is a different design. Dutch admission to a non-selective programme is an entitlement: hold a qualifying diploma, apply by the deadline, and you are in. Where demand exceeds places, the institution runs its own selection on its own criteria, which may weigh grades alongside a motivation letter, a test or an interview. So the question shifts from "what average do I need" to "is this programme selective, and what does that institution actually select on".
attribution: Nuffic's education-system pages for the IB
whatThisIsNot: Not a claim that grades do not matter. They matter a great deal in numerus fixus selection — they are simply not converted to a national scale first.
